items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: And Nick gave me a few jobs here and there, not steady, because he had his favorites.

ctx.x: That he could do it. Very few can do it today, in my opinion, again. But anyway, I'm finally at Rind's and I'm finally invited to play, one Sunday afternoon. It wasn't a big deal. I think I paid either seven or ten dollars. I remember playing City College and I hired Eddie Condon, Mezz Crow, Cliff Jackson, Frankie Newton and Dave Tough at seven dollars apiece, on Collins Stage, and I got ten for being leader and getting them together.

This was money in those days. You could still hire most musicians up til '46, say, '47, for a paltry -- Nick's paid no more than $40 a week. If you could get your money. Many times the guys waited weeks or -- for their money, they're always behind, oh, yes.
That's startling because of the publicity about Nick's. Known all over the world and the guys that played there become --
